title: Show HN: Geneva, a Rust FFmpeg CLI alternative with HTML/CSS graphics
text:
I built this for my own use case, and I think other people could benefit from it.

It's essentially a Rust rewrite of the ffmpeg CLI command, but with a modern API and good defaults + a native HTML/CSS composition engine that's been fine tuned for speed and memory efficiency. Under the hood, it still uses the libav* codecs from ffmpeg, so it can still work on a variety of formats.

Works very well with AI agents too: prompt what kind or intro/animation/graphics you need (or give it a reference), let the LLM come up with the HTML/CSS for it (Opus 5.5 is quite good at this), and let it use them on geneva.

It's way faster than the usual alternatives for putting still or animated graphics on videos (remotion, playwright etc.) because it doesn't use a browser or chromium. Everything is rendered natively, in a single pass.

I don't disagree with your other points, but calling Rust fast at compile time is... questionable.

I've been doing Rust full time for the last half-decade and hobby before that, and its slow compile times have always been a pain point.

And I've found its slow cycle around compile-then-test is a real pain point with agentic development. Agents get into loops trying things out, and verifying their results, and they tend to accumulate a pile of tests on top of that (which require periodic cleanup). Forward progress often gets successively more slow and painful as compile times start to dominate most of what the agent is doing.

For application -- not systems dev work -- I've been considering making a move to using something like OCaml instead.
